q: 我昨天吃___两片药。
zh: 我昨天吃了两片药。
py: wǒ zuó tiān chī le liǎng piàn yào
en: I took two tablets yesterday.
why: One finished act with a counted object: 了 goes right after 吃, before 两片. 着 describes a continuing state and 的 or 地 cannot mark a completed act at all.

q: 医生昨天给他开___三天的药。
zh: 医生昨天给他开了三天的药。
py: yī shēng zuó tiān gěi tā kāi le sān tiān de yào
en: The doctor prescribed him three days' worth of medicine yesterday.
why: A single finished prescription with a counted quantity: 了 sits right after 开, before 三天. 着 would make it a continuing state, which is wrong for one finished act.

q: 昨天夜里下___一场大雪，今天地上全是白的。
zh: 昨天夜里下了一场大雪，今天地上全是白的。
py: zuó tiān yè lǐ xià le yī chǎng dà xuě jīn tiān dì shang quán shì bái de
en: A heavy snow fell last night, and today the ground is all white.
why: One completed snowfall counted as 一场: 了 goes right after 下. 着 would describe snow that is still falling, but the snow has stopped and left the ground white.

q: 昨天他发烧，一口气喝___三大杯热水，然后就睡了。
zh: 昨天他发烧，一口气喝了三大杯热水，然后就睡了。
py: zuó tiān tā fā shāo yī kǒu qì hē le sān dà bēi rè shuǐ rán hòu jiù shuì le
en: Yesterday he had a fever; he downed three big glasses of hot water in one go and then went to sleep.
why: A finished drinking of a counted amount, followed by the next event: 了 right after 喝. 着 would mean he was drinking while doing something else, and 过 would put it in a vague experience past.

q: 今天早上小李跑___五公里，现在腿很疼。
zh: 今天早上小李跑了五公里，现在腿很疼。
py: jīn tiān zǎo shang xiǎo lǐ pǎo le wǔ gōng lǐ xiàn zài tuǐ hěn téng
en: Xiao Li ran five kilometres this morning and his legs hurt now.
why: A bounded distance (五公里) run and finished this morning: 了 goes right after 跑 and before the number. 着 would describe a running that is still in progress, which does not fit 现在腿很疼.

q: 昨天我买___那瓶退烧药，可是还没吃。
zh: 昨天我买了那瓶退烧药，可是还没吃。
py: zuó tiān wǒ mǎi le nà píng tuì shāo yào kě shì hái méi chī
en: I bought that bottle of fever medicine yesterday, but I have not taken it yet.
why: A specific object (那瓶退烧药) can follow 了 directly: the buying is one finished event. Leaving 了 out would sound like a plan, and 过 would mean an earlier experience, not yesterday.

q: 昨天还很热，今天天气冷___。
zh: 昨天还很热，今天天气冷了。
py: zuó tiān hái hěn rè jīn tiān tiān qì lěng le
en: It was still hot yesterday, but it has turned cold today.
why: 昨天还很热 sets up a contrast: it is cold now and was not before, so the sentence closes with 了. 着 and 过 do not mark a new state, and 呢 would only stress that it is still so.

q: 春天到___，花都开了。
zh: 春天到了，花都开了。
py: chūn tiān dào le huā dōu kāi le
en: Spring has arrived, and the flowers are all in bloom.
why: The arrival of spring is a new situation, so 了 closes the clause. 着 and 的 cannot report an arrival, and 过 would only mean spring had come at some earlier time.

q: 他的感冒好___，不用再吃药了。
zh: 他的感冒好了，不用再吃药了。
py: tā de gǎn mào hǎo le bù yòng zài chī yào le
en: His cold has cleared up; he does not need to take medicine any more.
why: 好了 reports a change (sick before, well now), and the next clause 不用再吃药 depends on it. 着 and 的 cannot mark a change, and 好过 would mean something like feeling better than before.

q: 快要下雪___，你出门别忘了戴帽子。
zh: 快要下雪了，你出门别忘了戴帽子。
py: kuài yào xià xuě le nǐ chū mén bié wàng le dài mào zi
en: It's about to snow, so don't forget your hat when you go out.
why: 快要 … 了 is the frame for something about to happen: 了 closes the clause. 过 or 着 cannot complete 快要, and 的 would turn the clause into a noun phrase.

q: 经过一个星期的治疗，他的咳嗽终于好___。
zh: 经过一个星期的治疗，他的咳嗽终于好了。
py: jīng guò yī ge xīng qī de zhì liáo tā de ké sou zhōng yú hǎo le
en: After a week of treatment, his cough has finally cleared up.
why: 终于 reports that a long-awaited change has happened, so the clause ends with 了. Without it the sentence stops short, 过 would mean it had cleared up earlier, and 着 cannot follow 好 here.

q: 树叶已经黄___，一阵风吹来就掉了。
zh: 树叶已经黄了，一阵风吹来就掉了。
py: shù yè yǐ jīng huáng le yī zhèn fēng chuī lái jiù diào le
en: The leaves have already turned yellow; one gust of wind and they fall.
why: 已经 plus an adjective reports a change that has taken place (green before, yellow now), so 了 comes at the end. 着 would say the leaves stay yellow, and 过 does not fit.

q: 雨停___，我们出去走走吧。
zh: 雨停了，我们出去走走吧。
py: yǔ tíng le wǒ men chū qù zǒu zou ba
en: The rain has stopped; let's go out for a walk.
why: The rain was falling and now is not, so the clause ends with 了. 着 and 的 cannot mark the stopping, and 停过 would say it had stopped at some earlier time.

q: 天越来越冷，医院里感冒的病人也多___。
zh: 天越来越冷，医院里感冒的病人也多了。
py: tiān yuè lái yuè lěng yī yuàn lǐ gǎn mào de bìng rén yě duō le
en: It's getting colder and colder, and there are more patients with colds in the hospital too.
why: 越来越 describes a change under way, so the matching result 多 ends with 了: there are more than before. 多 alone would be a plain description without the change, and 过 does not fit.

q: 孩子的烧退___，现在不烫了。
zh: 孩子的烧退了，现在不烫了。
py: hái zi de shāo tuì le xiàn zài bù tàng le
en: The child's fever has gone down; he isn't hot to the touch any more.
why: The fever was high and has now dropped, so 退 takes final 了. 着, 的 and 地 cannot mark a completed change of state.

q: 这场雨都下了三天___，还是没有停的意思。
zh: 这场雨都下了三天了，还是没有停的意思。
py: zhè chǎng yǔ dōu xià le sān tiān le hái shi méi yǒu tíng de yì si
en: It has been raining for three whole days and shows no sign of stopping.
why: 都 and 还是没有停 say the rain is still going, so the amount "so far" takes a second 了 at the end. 过 and 着 cannot close it.

q: 他已经发烧了三天___，一直没退，今天一定得去医院。
zh: 他已经发烧了三天了，一直没退，今天一定得去医院。
py: tā yǐ jīng fā shāo le sān tiān le yī zhí méi tuì jīn tiān yī dìng děi qù yī yuàn
en: He has already had a fever for three days and it has not gone down; he has to go to the hospital today.
why: The fever has lasted three days and is still there: 了 after the verb and 了 again at the end (已经 … 了). 过 or 着 would not give the "so far" reading.

q: 去年冬天我感冒了两个星期___，后来才好。
zh: 去年冬天我感冒了两个星期，后来才好。
py: qù nián dōng tiān wǒ gǎn mào le liǎng ge xīng qī hòu lái cái hǎo
en: Last winter I had a cold for two weeks before I got better.
why: 去年冬天 and 后来才好 close the period: the two weeks are over, so only the verb 了 is used. A final 了 would say the cold is still going on, which clashes with 后来才好.

q: 他在医院里住___半个月___，上个星期才回家。
zh: 他在医院里住了半个月，上个星期才回家。
py: tā zài yī yuàn lǐ zhù le bàn ge yuè shàng ge xīng qī cái huí jiā
en: He spent half a month in hospital and only came home last week.
why: 上个星期才回家 shows the stay is over, so the amount takes only the 了 after the verb. A second 了 would mean he is still in hospital, and dropping the first 了 leaves the finished stay unmarked.

q: 到现在他已经跑了五公里___，还不想停下来。
zh: 到现在他已经跑了五公里了，还不想停下来。
py: dào xiàn zài tā yǐ jīng pǎo le wǔ gōng lǐ le hái bù xiǎng tíng xià lái
en: By now he has already run five kilometres and still does not want to stop.
why: 到现在 and 还不想停 mean the running is still going, so the amount so far takes a second 了 at the end. 过, 着 and 的 cannot close the clause in this reading.

q: 小时候我在乡下住___十年___，所以特别喜欢那里的空气。
zh: 小时候我在乡下住了十年，所以特别喜欢那里的空气。
py: xiǎo shí hou wǒ zài xiāng xià zhù le shí nián suǒ yǐ tè bié xǐ huan nà lǐ de kōng qì
en: I lived in the countryside for ten years as a child, so I especially like the air there.
why: 小时候 closes the period: the ten years are over, so only the verb 了 is used. A second 了 would say he is still living there, and with no 了 at all the finished stay is not marked.

q: 这个冬天已经下了五场雪___，路上的雪还没化完。
zh: 这个冬天已经下了五场雪了，路上的雪还没化完。
py: zhè ge dōng tiān yǐ jīng xià le wǔ chǎng xuě le lù shàng de xuě hái méi huà wán
en: This winter it has already snowed five times, and the snow on the road has not all melted yet.
why: This winter is still going on, so the count is "so far": 了 after 下 and 了 again at the end (已经 … 了). 过 or 着 would not give a running total.

q: 他昨晚吃___两片药就睡了。
zh: 他昨晚吃了两片药就睡了。
py: tā zuó wǎn chī le liǎng piàn yào jiù shuì le
en: Last night he took two tablets and went to sleep.
why: In "after A, then B" with a counted object, 了 goes right after the first verb. 着 would mean he was taking pills while going to bed, and 的 or 地 cannot mark the completed first step.

q: 小王昨天吃___那两片退烧药就躺下了。
zh: 小王昨天吃了那两片退烧药就躺下了。
py: xiǎo wáng zuó tiān chī le nà liǎng piàn tuì shāo yào jiù tǎng xià le
en: Xiao Wang took those two fever tablets yesterday and lay down.
why: The first step is finished before the next one starts, so 了 follows 吃 and precedes the specific object. 着 would turn it into an action still in progress while lying down.

q: 我洗___三次手，才开始吃饭。
zh: 我洗了三次手，才开始吃饭。
py: wǒ xǐ le sān cì shǒu cái kāi shǐ chī fàn
en: I washed my hands three times before I started eating.
why: Hand-washing is a bounded, finished action (三次) that comes before eating, so 了 goes after 洗. 着 would mean washing while eating, which does not fit 才开始吃饭.

q: 你喝___这两杯热水，再休息一会儿吧。
zh: 你喝了这两杯热水，再休息一会儿吧。
py: nǐ hē le zhè liǎng bēi rè shuǐ zài xiū xi yī huì r ba
en: Drink these two cups of hot water first, then rest for a while.
why: In "do A, then B" even for a future request, 了 goes right after the first verb to mean once A is done. 着 would mean resting while drinking, and 的 or 地 mark nothing here.

q: 吃___饭，我们去公园散步。
zh: 吃了饭，我们去公园散步。
py: chī le fàn wǒ men qù gōng yuán sàn bù
en: After we eat, let's go for a walk in the park.
why: "Once A is done, B": 了 goes straight after the first verb, 吃. 着 would mean walking while eating, and 的 or 地 cannot appear after the verb here.

q: 你先量___体温，再决定要不要吃药。
zh: 你先量了体温，再决定要不要吃药。
py: nǐ xiān liáng le tǐ wēn zài jué dìng yào bù yào chī yào
en: Take your temperature first, then decide whether to take medicine.
why: 先 … 再 describes two steps in order, and 了 after the first verb says that step must be done before the second begins. 着 would mean doing both at once.

q: 等天气暖和___，我们就带孩子去公园放风筝。
zh: 等天气暖和了，我们就带孩子去公园放风筝。
py: děng tiān qì nuǎn huo le wǒ men jiù dài hái zi qù gōng yuán fàng fēng zheng
en: Once the weather warms up, we will take the children to the park to fly kites.
why: 等 … 了 … 就 means once the change has happened, even though it is in the future. 着 and 的 cannot mark that change, and 过 would put it in the past.

q: 我昨晚喝___那碗姜汤，出___一身汗，今天早上感觉好多了。
zh: 我昨晚喝了那碗姜汤，出了一身汗，今天早上感觉好多了。
py: wǒ zuó wǎn hē le nà wǎn jiāng tāng chū le yī shēn hàn jīn tiān zǎo shang gǎn jué hǎo duō le
en: Last night I drank that bowl of ginger soup and broke into a sweat; this morning I feel much better.
why: Both steps are finished events: 喝了那碗姜汤 and 出了一身汗. 着 would mean the drinking was still going on, and a 着 after 出 would not give a finished sweat.

q: 我每天早上喝___一杯热水。
zh: 我每天早上喝一杯热水。
py: wǒ měi tiān zǎo shang hē yī bēi rè shuǐ
en: I drink a cup of hot water every morning.
why: 每天 makes this a routine, not one finished event, so 了 is left out even though 一杯 is a counted object. 了 would turn it into a single completed drinking.

q: 小时候妈妈经常给我煮___姜汤。
zh: 小时候妈妈经常给我煮姜汤。
py: xiǎo shí hou mā ma jīng cháng gěi wǒ zhǔ jiāng tāng
en: When I was little, my mum often made me ginger soup.
why: 经常 marks a repeated habit, and a habit in the past still takes no 了. English past tense tempts you to add it, but 小时候 already puts it in the past.

q: 夏天他常常喝___冰水，所以总是拉肚子。
zh: 夏天他常常喝冰水，所以总是拉肚子。
py: xià tiān tā cháng cháng hē bīng shuǐ suǒ yǐ zǒng shì lā dù zi
en: In summer he often drinks iced water, so he often has an upset stomach.
why: 常常 and 总是 describe a repeated pattern, so the verb stays bare. 了 would turn it into one completed drinking, which contradicts the habit.

q: 那几年每到秋天，奶奶都要腌___很多萝卜，一直吃到春天。
zh: 那几年每到秋天，奶奶都要腌很多萝卜，一直吃到春天。
py: nà jǐ nián měi dào qiū tiān nǎi nai dōu yào yān hěn duō luó bo yī zhí chī dào chūn tiān
en: In those years, every autumn Grandma would pickle lots of radishes, and we ate them until spring.
why: 每到秋天 and 都要 describe a yearly routine, so no 了 even though the object is quantified (很多萝卜). 了 would make it one completed pickling.

q: 我们一般晚上八点吃___药。
zh: 我们一般晚上八点吃药。
py: wǒ men yī bān wǎn shang bā diǎn chī yào
en: We usually take our medicine at eight in the evening.
why: 一般 marks a regular habit, so the verb takes no 了. 了 would report one completed event, and 过 would mean having taken it at some earlier time.

q: 我昨天没吃___早饭。
zh: 我昨天没吃早饭。
py: wǒ zuó tiān méi chī zǎo fàn
en: I didn't have breakfast yesterday.
why: 没 already says the action did not happen, so there is nothing left for 了 to mark. 没吃了 is never right for "did not eat", and 没吃过 would mean never having eaten.

q: 医生让我吃药，可是我没吃___那些药。
zh: 医生让我吃药，可是我没吃那些药。
py: yī shēng ràng wǒ chī yào kě shì wǒ méi chī nà xiē yào
en: The doctor told me to take medicine, but I didn't take those pills.
why: A negated past action is 没 + verb, with no 了 after it. 没吃了 cannot mean "did not eat"; 着 and 的 do not belong here at all.

q: 昨天一整天都没下___雨，天气特别好。
zh: 昨天一整天都没下雨，天气特别好。
py: zuó tiān yī zhěng tiān dōu méi xià yǔ tiān qì tè bié hǎo
en: It did not rain all day yesterday, and the weather was great.
why: 没下雨 reports that rain did not occur, and 没 rules out 了. 没下了雨 is never right as "did not rain", and 着 or 的 do not fit.

q: 虽然医生让他多休息，但是他昨天一点儿也没休息___。
zh: 虽然医生让他多休息，但是他昨天一点儿也没休息。
py: suī rán yī shēng ràng tā duō xiū xi dàn shì tā zuó tiān yī diǎn r yě méi xiū xi
en: Although the doctor told him to rest more, he did not rest at all yesterday.
why: 一点儿也没 is a strong negative of a past action, and with 没 there is no 了 anywhere in the clause. 了 would contradict the denial that the resting happened.

q: 感冒的时候他没去___学校，一直在家休息。
zh: 感冒的时候他没去学校，一直在家休息。
py: gǎn mào de shí hou tā méi qù xué xiào yī zhí zài jiā xiū xi
en: When he had a cold he did not go to school and stayed home to rest.
why: 没去 says he did not go, so 了 must be dropped. 去了 would say he went, which is the opposite of the sentence.

q: 去年冬天北京很冷___，我每天都穿羽绒服。
zh: 去年冬天北京很冷，我每天都穿羽绒服。
py: qù nián dōng tiān běi jīng hěn lěng wǒ měi tiān dōu chuān yǔ róng fú
en: Last winter Beijing was very cold, and I wore a down jacket every day.
why: This describes how things were, not a change, and 去年冬天 already shows it is past. 很冷了 would announce that it has newly turned cold, which is not the point.

q: 我小时候很怕___打针，每次都哭。
zh: 我小时候很怕打针，每次都哭。
py: wǒ xiǎo shí hou hěn pà dǎ zhēn měi cì dōu kū
en: When I was little I was very afraid of injections and cried every time.
why: 怕 is a state, and 小时候 with 每次都 shows a past habit of feeling, so no 了. Adding 了 after 怕 would suggest a sudden event rather than a lasting feeling.

q: 医生昨天觉得___我的病不严重，让我回家休息。
zh: 医生昨天觉得我的病不严重，让我回家休息。
py: yī shēng zuó tiān jué de wǒ de bìng bù yán zhòng ràng wǒ huí jiā xiū xi
en: The doctor thought my illness wasn't serious and sent me home to rest.
why: 觉得 is a thought state; the past comes from 昨天, and 觉得了 is never used to mean "thought". 了 only fits a new realisation at the end of a clause, not directly after 觉得.

q: 昨天下午公园里有___很多人，大家都在晒太阳。
zh: 昨天下午公园里有很多人，大家都在晒太阳。
py: zuó tiān xià wǔ gōng yuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō rén dà jiā dōu zài shài tài yáng
en: There were lots of people in the park yesterday afternoon, all sunning themselves.
why: 有 describes what existed, which is a state, so it takes no 了; 昨天下午 shows the past. 过 would mean "have been" in some earlier time, and 着 does not belong here.

q: 他以前是___我们学校最好的游泳运动员，现在腿受伤了。
zh: 他以前是我们学校最好的游泳运动员，现在腿受伤了。
py: tā yǐ qián shì wǒ men xué xiào zuì hǎo de yóu yǒng yùn dòng yuán xiàn zài tuǐ shòu shāng le
en: He used to be the best swimmer at our school, but now his leg is injured.
why: 是 is never followed by 了 to mean "was"; 以前 carries the past. The final 了 in 受伤了 is a separate, correct change-of-state 了.

q: 我那时候很喜欢___夏天，因为可以天天游泳。
zh: 我那时候很喜欢夏天，因为可以天天游泳。
py: wǒ nà shí hou hěn xǐ huan xià tiān yīn wèi kě yǐ tiān tiān yóu yǒng
en: Back then I really liked summer, because I could swim every day.
why: 喜欢 is a feeling, and 那时候 supplies the past, so no 了. 喜欢了 would suggest I had just come to like it.

q: 今天太热___，我们别出去了。
zh: 今天太热了，我们别出去了。
py: jīn tiān tài rè le wǒ men bié chū qù le
en: It's too hot today; let's not go out.
why: A remark with 太 + adjective closes with 了: 太热了. 的, 着 and 过 cannot finish a 太 remark.

q: 这种药太苦___，孩子不愿意吃。
zh: 这种药太苦了，孩子不愿意吃。
py: zhè zhǒng yào tài kǔ le hái zi bù yuàn yì chī
en: This medicine is too bitter; the child won't take it.
why: 太 + adjective at the end of a clause takes 了: 太苦了. Without 了 the remark sounds cut off, and 的, 着 or 过 are not used after the adjective.

q: 太冷___的天气我不想出门。
zh: 太冷的天气我不想出门。
py: tài lěng de tiān qì wǒ bù xiǎng chū mén
en: I don't want to go out in weather that is too cold.
why: Here 太冷 is only a modifier inside a longer noun phrase (太冷的天气), so it takes no 了; 了 belongs to 太 remarks that end the clause. 太冷了的天气 is not a Chinese phrase.

q: 医生说你的身体太弱___，必须多休息。
zh: 医生说你的身体太弱了，必须多休息。
py: yī shēng shuō nǐ de shēn tǐ tài ruò le bì xū duō xiū xi
en: The doctor says your body is too weak and you must rest more.
why: A complete remark with 太 + adjective ends with 了: 太弱了. 的, 着 and 过 cannot close it, and without any particle the remark sounds incomplete.

q: 我头不疼___，可以去上课了。
zh: 我头不疼了，可以去上课了。
py: wǒ tóu bù téng le kě yǐ qù shàng kè le
en: My head does not hurt any more; I can go to class now.
why: "No longer" is 不 + verb + 了: it hurt before, and now it does not. 过, 着 and 地 cannot mark that change.

q: 雨太大了，我们不去爬山___。
zh: 雨太大了，我们不去爬山了。
py: yǔ tài dà le wǒ men bù qù pá shān le
en: The rain is too heavy; we're not going hiking after all.
why: A changed plan is 不 + verb + 了: we meant to go and now are not going. 过, 着 and 地 cannot express "after all".

q: 他已经戒烟了，现在不抽烟___。
zh: 他已经戒烟了，现在不抽烟了。
py: tā yǐ jīng jiè yān le xiàn zài bù chōu yān le
en: He has quit smoking and doesn't smoke any more.
why: 已经 and 现在 say the situation has changed, so 不抽烟 takes 了 at the end: he did smoke before, and does not now. 过, 着 and 地 cannot mark "any more".

q: 退烧药都吃完了，家里没有药___。
zh: 退烧药都吃完了，家里没有药了。
py: tuì shāo yào dōu chī wán le jiā lǐ méi yǒu yào le
en: The fever medicine is all gone; there is no medicine left in the house.
why: 没有 + noun + 了 means "none left": there was some, now there is not. 过, 着 and 地 do not mark that change.

q: 天太冷了，爷爷说他今天不想出门___。
zh: 天太冷了，爷爷说他今天不想出门了。
py: tiān tài lěng le yé ye shuō tā jīn tiān bù xiǎng chū mén le
en: It's so cold that Grandpa says he doesn't want to go out today after all.
why: The cold has changed his mind: 不想出门 + 了 means he no longer wants to go. 过, 着 and 地 cannot express a change of plan.

zh: 我昨天喝了三杯热水。
py: wǒ zuó tiān hē le sān bēi rè shuǐ
en: I drank three cups of hot water yesterday.
why: 了 goes right after 喝, before the counted object 三杯热水. The time word 昨天 can come before or after the subject.

zh: 今天天气暖和了。
py: jīn tiān tiān qì nuǎn huo le
en: The weather has warmed up today.
why: The change of state is closed by 了 at the very end. 了 cannot sit before 暖和, and the time word may come before or after 天气.

zh: 下个月天气就要变冷了。
py: xià ge yuè tiān qì jiù yào biàn lěng le
en: The weather will turn cold next month.
why: 就要 … 了 frames something about to happen, so 了 must end the sentence. 下个月 may come before or after 天气.

zh: 我咳嗽了一个星期了。
py: wǒ ké sou le yī ge xīng qī le
en: I have been coughing for a week now.
why: For "so far, and still going" the first 了 follows the verb and the second closes the sentence. The duration 一个星期 sits between them.

zh: 这里已经下了一个星期的雨了。
py: zhè lǐ yǐ jīng xià le yī ge xīng qī de yǔ le
en: It has already been raining here for a week.
why: 已经 plus a duration that is still running needs 了 after the verb and 了 at the end. 这里 may come before or after 已经.

zh: 我吃了两片药就睡觉。
py: wǒ chī le liǎng piàn yào jiù shuì jiào
en: I'll go to sleep once I've taken two tablets.
why: In "after A, then B", 了 goes right after the first verb 吃, before the counted object 两片药, and 就 introduces the second step.

zh: 他昨天洗了热水澡就睡了。
py: tā zuó tiān xǐ le rè shuǐ zǎo jiù shuì le
en: Yesterday he took a hot bath and went straight to bed.
why: The first step takes 了 right after the verb, and a past sequence is closed by a second 了 at the end. 昨天 may come before or after 他.

zh: 你量了体温再决定吃不吃药。
py: nǐ liáng le tǐ wēn zài jué dìng chī bù chī yào
en: Take your temperature first, then decide whether to take medicine.
why: 再 means only after the first step is done, so the first verb 量 carries 了 before its object 体温. 了 cannot move to the end.

zh: 今天的风太大了。
py: jīn tiān de fēng tài dà le
en: The wind is too strong today.
why: 太 + adjective + 了 closes the remark, so 了 comes last. The noun phrase 今天的风 must stay together at the front.

zh: 我现在不吃甜的了。
py: wǒ xiàn zài bù chī tián de le
en: I don't eat sweet things any more.
why: "Not any more" is 不 + verb + object + 了, with 了 last. 现在 may come before or after 我.

zh: 因为下雨，他今天不来了。
py: yīn wèi xià yǔ tā jīn tiān bù lái le
en: Because it's raining, he is not coming today after all.
why: The changed plan 不来 takes 了 at the end. The reason clause 因为下雨 stays first, and 今天 may come before or after 他.

zh: 我昨天没吃退烧药。
py: wǒ zuó tiān méi chī tuì shāo yào
en: I didn't take any fever medicine yesterday.
why: 没 goes before the verb and no 了 appears, so the spare tile 了 is not used. 昨天 may come before or after 我.

zh: 去年冬天北京很冷。
py: qù nián dōng tiān běi jīng hěn lěng
en: Beijing was very cold last winter.
why: A past state is described with 很 + adjective and no 了; the time phrase already shows it is past. The spare tile 了 is not used.

zh: 我每天晚上都喝一杯牛奶。
py: wǒ měi tiān wǎn shang dōu hē yī bēi niú nǎi
en: I drink a glass of milk every evening.
why: 每天晚上 marks a routine, so the verb takes no 了 even with the counted object 一杯. The spare tile 了 is not used.

zh: 我们都等了半个小时了，医生还没来。
py: wǒ men dōu děng le bàn ge xiǎo shí le yī shēng hái méi lái
en: We have been waiting for half an hour and the doctor still hasn't come.
why: The wait is still going, so the amount takes 了 after the verb and 了 at the end of its clause. The two clauses can swap places.

src_py: wǒ zuó tiān qù yī yuàn le
zh: 我昨天没去医院。
py: wǒ zuó tiān méi qù yī yuàn
en: I didn't go to the hospital yesterday.
why: To say it did not happen, use 没 + verb and drop 了. 不去了 would mean a changed plan instead.

src_py: tā hē le nà bēi jiāng tāng
zh: 他没喝那杯姜汤。
py: tā méi hē nà bēi jiāng tāng
en: He didn't drink that cup of ginger soup.
why: Negate a finished action with 没 and delete 了. 他没喝了那杯姜汤 is wrong.

src_py: tā měi tiān hē bīng shuǐ
task: Say he doesn't drink it any more.
zh: 他不喝冰水了。
py: tā bù hē bīng shuǐ le
en: He doesn't drink iced water any more.
why: "Not any more" is 不 + verb + object + 了. 没喝 would only say he did not drink on some occasion.

src: 下雨了，我们明天去爬山。
src_py: xià yǔ le wǒ men míng tiān qù pá shān
task: Say we are not going hiking any more.
zh: 下雨了，我们不去爬山了。
py: xià yǔ le wǒ men bù qù pá shān le
en: It's raining, so we're not going hiking any more.
why: A cancelled plan is 不 + verb + 了, with 了 at the end. 没去 would report a past fact, not a changed decision.

task: Say the weather has turned hot (a change).
zh: 天气热了。
py: tiān qì rè le
en: The weather has turned hot.
why: To report a change, drop 很 and close with 了: 热了. 很热 is only a plain description.

src_py: tā xǐ rè shuǐ zǎo rán hòu shuì jiào
task: Join with 就: once he has bathed, he goes to bed.
zh: 他洗了热水澡就睡觉。
py: tā xǐ le rè shuǐ zǎo jiù shuì jiào
en: He goes to bed as soon as he has had a hot bath.
why: The first step takes 了 right after 洗, and 就 introduces the second. Both 了 positions are heard, but 了 must come before 就.

src_py: yǔ tíng yǐ hòu wǒ men qù pá shān
task: Use 了 and 就 for 'once the rain has stopped'.
zh: 雨停了，我们就去爬山。
py: yǔ tíng le wǒ men jiù qù pá shān
en: Once the rain stops, we will go hiking.
why: "Once A is done, B": 了 after the first verb and 就 before the second. 以后 is replaced by 了 + 就.

src: 他在医院里住了一个月。
src_py: tā zài yī yuàn lǐ zhù le yī ge yuè
task: Say he has been in hospital for a month so far and is still there.
zh: 他在医院里已经住了一个月了。
py: tā zài yī yuàn lǐ yǐ jīng zhù le yī ge yuè le
en: He has already been in hospital for a month.
why: For "so far, and still going" add a second 了 at the end after the amount. The single-了 source is a finished stay.

src_py: tā jīn tiān zǎo shang hē shuǐ
task: Say she drank two glasses of water this morning (finished).
zh: 她今天早上喝了两杯水。
py: tā jīn tiān zǎo shang hē le liǎng bēi shuǐ
en: She drank two glasses of water this morning.
why: A finished act with a counted object puts 了 right after 喝, before 两杯. The time phrase may come before or after 她.

src_py: zhè jiàn yǔ róng fú hěn guì
zh: 这件羽绒服太贵了！
py: zhè jiàn yǔ róng fú tài guì le
en: This down jacket is too expensive!
why: A 太 remark ends with 了: 太贵了. 很 does not take 了 in this way.

s: 昨天很热了，我们都没出门。
s_py: zuó tiān hěn rè le wǒ men dōu méi chū mén
zh: 昨天很热，我们都没出门。
py: zuó tiān hěn rè wǒ men dōu méi chū mén
en: It was very hot yesterday, so none of us went out.
why: A past description with 很 + adjective takes no 了; 昨天 already shows it is past. 很热了 would announce a change that is not meant here.

s: 我昨天没去了医院。
s_py: wǒ zuó tiān méi qù le yī yuàn
zh: 我昨天没去医院。
py: wǒ zuó tiān méi qù yī yuàn
en: I didn't go to the hospital yesterday.
why: 没 already says the action did not happen, so 了 cannot follow the verb. 没去了 is never correct.

s: 小时候我每天都喝了牛奶。
s_py: xiǎo shí hou wǒ měi tiān dōu hē le niú nǎi
zh: 小时候我每天都喝牛奶。
py: xiǎo shí hou wǒ měi tiān dōu hē niú nǎi
en: When I was little I drank milk every day.
why: 每天都 makes this a habit, and a habit takes no 了 even in the past. 了 would present it as one finished drinking.

s: 这碗汤太了烫，我喝不了。
s_py: zhè wǎn tāng tài le tàng wǒ hē bù liǎo
zh: 这碗汤太烫了，我喝不了。
py: zhè wǎn tāng tài tàng le wǒ hē bù liǎo
en: This soup is too hot; I can't drink it.
why: In a 太 remark 了 closes the clause after the adjective: 太烫了. It cannot be inserted between 太 and 烫.

s: 太冷了，我们没去公园了。
s_py: tài lěng le wǒ men méi qù gōng yuán le
zh: 太冷了，我们不去公园了。
py: tài lěng le wǒ men bù qù gōng yuán le
en: It's too cold; we're not going to the park after all.
why: A changed decision is 不 + verb + 了. 没去 reports a fact about the past and cannot be followed by 了 here.

s: 他以前是了我们的校医。
s_py: tā yǐ qián shì le wǒ men de xiào yī
zh: 他以前是我们的校医。
py: tā yǐ qián shì wǒ men de xiào yī
en: He used to be our school doctor.
why: 是 is a state, so it never takes 了 to mean "was"; 以前 already carries the past.

s: 我昨天买三件羽绒服。
s_py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi sān jiàn yǔ róng fú
zh: 我昨天买了三件羽绒服。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi le sān jiàn yǔ róng fú
en: I bought three down jackets yesterday.
why: One finished purchase with a counted object needs 了 right after the verb. 昨天 gives the time but cannot replace 了.

s: 医生说他还没好了，需要再住几天院。
s_py: yī shēng shuō tā hái méi hǎo le xū yào zài zhù jǐ tiān yuàn
zh: 医生说他还没好，需要再住几天院。
py: yī shēng shuō tā hái méi hǎo xū yào zài zhù jǐ tiān yuàn
en: The doctor says he isn't better yet and needs to stay in hospital a few more days.
why: 还没 says something has not happened yet, so it cannot be closed with 了, which would claim a change. The sentence needs the bare 还没好.

s: 我觉得了那个医生很年轻。
s_py: wǒ jué de le nà ge yī shēng hěn nián qīng
zh: 我觉得那个医生很年轻。
py: wǒ jué de nà ge yī shēng hěn nián qīng
en: I think that doctor is very young.
why: 觉得 is a mental state, and 了 cannot follow it. 我觉得了 is not a Chinese way to say "I thought".

s: 以前我常常迟到了。
s_py: yǐ qián wǒ cháng cháng chí dào le
zh: 以前我常常迟到。
py: yǐ qián wǒ cháng cháng chí dào
en: I used to be late often.
why: 常常 marks a repeated habit, so no 了, even though 以前 is in the past. A final 了 would present it as a new development.

s: 我三天没睡好觉了，头特别疼。
s_py: wǒ sān tiān méi shuì hǎo jiào le tóu tè bié téng
zh: 我三天没睡好觉了，头特别疼。
py: wǒ sān tiān méi shuì hǎo jiào le tóu tè bié téng
en: I haven't slept properly for three days and my head aches badly.
why: This is correct: duration + 没 + verb + 了 is a fixed pattern for "has not ... for three days (up to now)". The 了 here marks the ongoing situation, not a completed action.

s: 昨天下了一天的雨，路上全是水。
s_py: zuó tiān xià le yī tiān de yǔ lù shàng quán shì shuǐ
zh: 昨天下了一天的雨，路上全是水。
py: zuó tiān xià le yī tiān de yǔ lù shàng quán shì shuǐ
en: It rained all day yesterday and the road is full of water.
why: This is correct: a finished event with a counted duration (一天) takes 了 right after the verb. 是 in the second clause is a plain description with no 了.

s: 我没有退烧药了，你有吗？
s_py: wǒ méi yǒu tuì shāo yào le nǐ yǒu ma
zh: 我没有退烧药了，你有吗？
py: wǒ méi yǒu tuì shāo yào le nǐ yǒu ma
en: I've run out of fever medicine; do you have any?
why: This is correct: 没有 + noun + 了 means "none left", a legitimate 没 … 了 pattern, unlike a negated finished action.

s: 我以前很怕冷，现在不怕了。
s_py: wǒ yǐ qián hěn pà lěng xiàn zài bù pà le
zh: 我以前很怕冷，现在不怕了。
py: wǒ yǐ qián hěn pà lěng xiàn zài bù pà le
en: I used to be very afraid of the cold; I'm not any more.
why: This is correct: the past state 很怕冷 takes no 了, while the new situation 不怕 takes 了 at the end.

s: 去年夏天这里特别热，我们天天都开着空调。
s_py: qù nián xià tiān zhè lǐ tè bié rè wǒ men tiān tiān dōu kāi zhe kōng tiáo
zh: 去年夏天这里特别热，我们天天都开着空调。
py: qù nián xià tiān zhè lǐ tè bié rè wǒ men tiān tiān dōu kāi zhe kōng tiáo
en: Last summer it was very hot here and we kept the air conditioning on every day.
why: This is correct: the hot weather is a past state and the routine is a habit, so neither takes 了. 着 shows the air conditioning stayed on.

s: 他每天早上起床以后先量体温。
s_py: tā měi tiān zǎo shang qǐ chuáng yǐ hòu xiān liáng tǐ wēn
zh: 他每天早上起床以后先量体温。
py: tā měi tiān zǎo shang qǐ chuáng yǐ hòu xiān liáng tǐ wēn
en: Every morning after getting up, he takes his temperature first.
why: This is correct: 以后 does not call for 了, because this is a daily routine and 每天 rules out 了 on either verb.

s: 秋天了，树叶都黄了。
s_py: qiū tiān le shù yè dōu huáng le
zh: 秋天了，树叶都黄了。
py: qiū tiān le shù yè dōu huáng le
en: It's autumn now, and the leaves have all turned yellow.
why: This is correct: 秋天了 reports that the season has changed, and 黄了 reports a change in the leaves. Both 了 mark new situations.

s: 你下了课就来我家吧，我给你煮姜汤。
s_py: nǐ xià le kè jiù lái wǒ jiā ba wǒ gěi nǐ zhǔ jiāng tāng
zh: 你下了课就来我家吧，我给你煮姜汤。
py: nǐ xià le kè jiù lái wǒ jiā ba wǒ gěi nǐ zhǔ jiāng tāng
en: Come to my place as soon as class is over, and I'll make you ginger soup.
why: This is correct: in "once A is done, B" 了 goes after the first verb even for a future request. 煮姜汤 is a plain future action with no 了.

s: 今天不太冷，你不用穿那么厚。
s_py: jīn tiān bù tài lěng nǐ bù yòng chuān nà me hòu
zh: 今天不太冷，你不用穿那么厚。
py: jīn tiān bù tài lěng nǐ bù yòng chuān nà me hòu
en: It's not very cold today; you don't need to wear so much.
why: This is correct: 不太 + adjective is a plain description and takes no 了; only 太 + adjective as a remark ends in 了.

s: 我都咳嗽了两个星期了，今天一定要去医院。
s_py: wǒ dōu ké sou le liǎng ge xīng qī le jīn tiān yī dìng yào qù yī yuàn
zh: 我都咳嗽了两个星期了，今天一定要去医院。
py: wǒ dōu ké sou le liǎng ge xīng qī le jīn tiān yī dìng yào qù yī yuàn
en: I've been coughing for two whole weeks; I'm definitely going to the hospital today.
why: This is correct: the cough is still going, so the amount so far takes two 了, one after the verb and one at the end, as 都 … 了 expects.
